aboutH2: Living Potential Inc.: Sober Living for Adults in Calgary, Alberta
intro: Living Potential Inc. is a sober living house in Calgary for adults in recovery from alcohol and drug addiction. It is a place to live, and the owners are clear that it is a peer-supported home and not clinical treatment: there is no detox, medical care or counselling on site. Guests rent a private furnished room, share the kitchen and living spaces, and keep up their own recovery through meetings, sponsors and outside supports.

Rent runs from $1,400 to $1,600 a month and includes groceries, household supplies and pre-made meals. The house works around day and night shifts, and guests are expected to be working, studying or keeping some steady routine while they get their footing back.

pillars.title: A Private Room in a Shared Calgary Home
pillars.body: Each guest has their own furnished room with fresh bedding, bright lighting and a new smart TV with streaming. There are three room types: a large room with a queen bed, a room with a double bed, desk and long dresser, and a smaller room with a double bed and a closet. Everyone shares the kitchen, bathrooms and living areas, and the photos on the house's website show a covered back deck with a barbecue and string lights. Wi-Fi, Netflix, Disney+, Prime and Crave are part of the rent.

pillars.title: Work, School and Recovery Meetings
pillars.body: Living Potential wants guests out in the world. People are strongly encouraged to hold a job, go to school or take on regular responsibilities, and the house is fine with day or night shifts. Groceries and household supplies are covered and there are always frozen meals ready, which takes some pressure off long workdays. Guests are also encouraged to go to recovery meetings and build ties with a sponsor, a psychologist and the recovery community in Calgary. The recovery.com profile mentions AA and NA meetings and an introduction to the 12 steps.

pillars.title: Case by Case, With Freedom and Accountability
pillars.body: The owners ran the house quietly for a few years before putting it on the map, and they chose a different style from stricter recovery housing. They look at each guest case by case. The idea is independence inside a structured home, meeting people where they are without judgement, and helping them ease back into ordinary life. For someone leaving a residential program in Calgary or elsewhere in Southern Alberta, it is a sober place to land while work and routines settle.

overview: Sober living sits between treatment and fully independent life. Living Potential puts it in plain terms: the goal is a safe, reasonable home that keeps stress and confusion down while people learn to live well without alcohol or drugs. In its own words, recovery is about building a stable, meaningful life, and abstinence is only part of that.

faqIntro: Answers come from the Living Potential website and its public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Living Potential Inc. a treatment centre?
faqs.a: No. Living Potential Inc. is a sober living house in Calgary, which it describes as a safe, supportive living environment for people in recovery. There is no detox, medical care or clinical treatment on site. Guests get a sober, structured place to live while they work, study and use meetings and outside supports.

faqs.q: How much does Living Potential cost?
faqs.a: Rooms cost $1,400, $1,500 or $1,600 a month, depending on the room, according to the Living Potential website. Every price includes food and management costs. The centre's recovery.com profile says it is private pay, and no insurance coverage is listed.

All rooms are private and furnished. The large room has a queen bed, dresser, closet and smart TV for $1,600 a month. The $1,500 room has a double bed, desk, long dresser and medium closet, and the small room has a double bed and small closet for $1,400. Kitchens, bathrooms and living areas are shared.
Yes. Groceries and household supplies are included in the rent. The fridge and pantry are stocked, and pre-made meals are kept in the freezer so guests can eat at any time of day.

faqs.q: Can I keep working while I live there?
faqs.a: Yes, and Living Potential encourages it. The house accommodates both night shift and day shift schedules. Guests are strongly encouraged to find work, go to school or take on regular daily responsibilities.

faqs.q: Do residents have to go to meetings?
faqs.a: Living Potential strongly encourages regular recovery meetings and building relationships with sponsors, psychologists and the wider recovery community. Its recovery.com profile lists an introduction to the 12-step program and AA and NA meetings. Ask the house directly about any meeting requirements.

faqs.q: Who can live at Living Potential?
faqs.a: The house is for adults working toward lasting sobriety from alcohol or drug addiction. Its recovery.com profile lists both men and women. Living Potential says it works with each guest case by case, so call to talk through your situation.

Living Potential does not publish a set length of stay, and rooms are rented by the month. The house says it works with guests case by case and aims for a smooth move back into everyday living. Ask about current availability when you call.

faqs.q: Where is Living Potential in Calgary?
faqs.a: The house is in Calgary, Alberta. The website and Google listing do not publish a street address, so you get the location when you contact the house. Airdrie is roughly 20 to 30 minutes from Calgary, and Red Deer is about 1.5 hours up Highway 2.

No public funding is mentioned. Living Potential Inc. is a privately run house, and its recovery.com profile lists private pay. If you need publicly funded addiction services in Alberta, those run through Recovery Alberta and funded beds at non-profit centres.

faqs.q: How do I get a room?
faqs.a: Call (587) 435-9643, email livingpotentialinc@gmail.com or leave your details on the contact form at livingpotentialinc.ca. A Living Potential representative will get back to you to talk about available rooms.
